independent_mathematical_scrutiny.regularity_minimality: The statement requires only the prescribed local scalarC² and the proof uses no global profile information, nonzero-radius guard or positive-dimension guard. LocalC² is a sufficient contract, not an assertion of logically weakest regularity. At a center, g(s)=s producesΔf=2d, while g(s)=s² producesΔf=0; the general proof keeps both cases. Merely knowing the composite is smooth cannot justify the formula with totalized scalar derivatives: g(s)=|s| is nonsmooth at 0 while g(||z||²)=||z||² is smooth, illustrating why a scalar derivative hypothesis matters. Thus n = 2 uses log, and q=2-n annihilates the power coefficient for n>2. Pairing with R⁻¹x gives1/R and(2-n)R^(1-n), respectively; no truncated natural subtraction or missingR factor occurs.
